subject: Post-call: RFQ evaluation playbook + open validation asks
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@mediq-systems.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 4 May 2025 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: RFQ evaluation playbook + open validation asks

Sanjay / Priya — thanks again for a productive call earlier. Quick recap + the playbook we discussed so your procurement + infra teams have a compact checklist for the bake-off. I attached the draft RFQ playbook and a short probe-specs PDF for the latency/throughput tests.

Summary of pain & goals (as I understand them):
- Pain: inconsistent inference latency across bursts; unpredictable token cost when spikes occur; lack of a path to run in VPC for PHI-handling.
- Goal: 99th/99.9th latency SLOs for user-facing flows, stable unit economics at scale, and an auditable private deployment for regulated workloads.

Decision criteria (ranked):
1) Tail latency under realistic traffic (99th/99.9th)
2) Cost per 1M tokens at expected QPS (including KV cache benefits)
3) Private deployment fit (VPC + KMS + audit logs)
4) Rollout controls: canary, automatic fallback, model pinning
5) Support / SLA & procurement terms

Open validation asks / next tests we agreed:
- Production-like latency probe: 30m continuous run with 95/99/99.9 measurements across three burst patterns. (Spec in attachment).
- KV/prefix cache warm-up test: measure cold->hot token cost delta and latency impact.
- Cost delta matrix: hosted vs dedicated (12 GPU) vs private on your Azure tenancy for your token mix.
- SOC2 evidence & data residency checklist for security review (we can package redacted artifacts).

Mutual action plan (draft dates):
- 5/6: Redwood sends final RFQ playbook & probe configs (attached).
- 5/9–5/12: Mediq runs a 2-day latency probe with Redwood-supplied harness (we provide scripts).
- 5/16: Joint runbook review and procurement term check-in.
- 5/23: Decision window for shortlist / procurement next steps.

Quick asks for your procurement team to unblock:
- Confirm target QPS range and representative promptset (sample prompts or a subset of logs).
- Confirm whether the bake-off needs to run inside your VPC or if a dedicated-hosted probe is acceptable for initial benchmarking.

Attachments: redwood-rfq-playbook-v1.xlsx (draft), latency-throughput-probe-specs.pdf

Thanks — I’ll be standing by to help the infra team run the harness.

Jonas Weber
Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 222-7811
[attachment: redwood-rfq-playbook-v1.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@mediq-systems.com>

Cc: Priya Das <priya.das@mediq-systems.com>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 May 2025 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: RFQ evaluation playbook + open validation asks

Jonas — thanks for the crisp recap. This is very helpful. A few clarifications from our side before we kick the probes: 

1) QPS / workload: Our primary user flow is the clinician triage assistant. Baseline average QPS ~ 60 sustained, spikes up to 300 for 30–90s. We can extract a 48-hour representative promptset (redacted) for the test.
2) VPC requirement: procurement prefers the bake-off start in our Azure tenancy under a private preview instance; if that’s infeasible for day-1 probes, we can accept a dedicated-hosted baseline run then repeat in our VPC for final verification.
3) SOC2: Procurement needs SOC2 Type II rolling reports and a contact for SOC evidence exchange.

We’ll aim to run the two-day probe on 5/9–5/10 as proposed but need the harness scripts by 5/6 EOD. Also sharing the lead infra contact: Priya Das (priya.das@mediq-systems.com).

—Sanjay
Head of Platform Engineering | Mediq Systems
[signature]

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Das <priya.das@mediq-systems.com>, Sanjay Rao <sanjay@mediq-systems.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 May 2025 17:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: RFQ evaluation playbook + open validation asks

Hi Priya / Sanjay — looping in our infra and product ops owners to make the technical checklist explicit. A few operational items we’ll own for the probe and what we need from you: 

What Redwood will provide (by 5/6 EOD):
- Probe harness (containerized) + runbook for Azure private preview and hosted inference runs.
- Pre-built scripts to collect 95/99/99.9 latency histograms, token counts, and cost breakdown.
- A trimmed probe promptset (we’ll anonymize if you share larger logs).
- SOC2 contact: security-qa@redwood.ai (we’ll put you in touch and send a redacted evidence bundle).

What we need from Mediq (please provide before 5/8):
- Representative promptset (48h sample) or a synthetic config that mimics your QPS spikes.
- Azure subscription details and an infra contact for private preview deployment (resource-group, vnet peering constraints, KMS ownership).
- Any contractual must-haves for procurement (e.g., mandatory SLAs, minimum indemnity language, or data residency clauses).

Open technical probes / acceptance criteria (for the bake-off):
- Tail latency: 95th < 120ms, 99th < 220ms, 99.9th < 420ms for the clinician triage prompts running at target QPS.
- Cost: hosted baseline must show at least a 20% delta improvement when running with KV cache enabled vs cold-run (we’ll provide a cost matrix).
- Failover: automatic fallback to a smaller variant must not increase median latency > 10% under synthetic load.

Attachment: small checklist and the probe spec. I’ll send the harness link once we push to the shared drive.

—Camila Reyes
Product Ops | Redwood Inference
[attachment: latency-throughput-probe-specs.pdf (application/pdf)]

Thanks all — great alignment. Quick confirmation: we’ll deliver the harness + playbook by 5/6 EOD and the SOC2 redacted bundle via security-qa@redwood.ai.

Action items for Redwood (owner):
- Jonas: finalize RFQ playbook and push to shared drive (5/6).
- Camila: deliver probe harness + run scripts (5/6).
- Marissa: prepare a short procurement summary with sample SLA redlines we typically propose (5/8).
- Karthik: prepare a short private-deployment checklist for Azure preview (5/8).

Action items for Mediq (owner):

- Sanjay: confirm representative promptset or give permission for synthetic generation (5/8).

I’ll follow up tomorrow with the Drive link and the initial probe run instructions. If any of the dates are tight on your side, flag now and we’ll adjust the window.

Appreciate the speed — looking forward to the tests.
